chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Uthman ibn Isa, from al-Sama'ah ibn Mahran, who said:

I asked him about faith and Islam, and I said to him: Do you differentiate between faith and Islam? He said: Shall I give you an example of it? I said: I would like that. He said: The example of faith from Islam is like the example of the Sacred Kaaba from the Sanctuary; a man may be in the Sanctuary and not be in the Kaaba, until he is in the Sanctuary. And he may be a Muslim and not be a believer, and he will not be a believer until he is a Muslim. I said: Then does anything exclude him from faith? He said to me: Yes. I said: Then to what does it turn him? He said: To Islam or disbelief. And he said: If a man enters the Kaaba and his urine slips from him, he is taken out of the Kaaba but does not go out of the Sanctuary. And if he goes out from the Sanctuary, washes his garment and purifies himself, he is not prevented from entering the Kaaba. But if a man enters the Kaaba and urinates in it intentionally, he is taken out of the Kaaba and from the Sanctuary, and his neck is struck.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Islam and faith (Iman) in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq employs the spatial analogy of the Kaaba within the broader Haram to illustrate the hierarchical relationship between Islam (submission) and Iman (faith), where Islam is the necessary container for Iman. The hadith further refines this by distinguishing between minor defects that may remove one from the perfection of faith while retaining Islam, and major, intentional sins that expel one from both states entirely, a nuance central to Shia theological discourse on the status of the sinner.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We told by Muhammed bin Hasan, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan al-Saffar, from Abbas bin Ma’ruf, from Uthman bin Isa, from Sama’a bin Mahran, that he said:

I asked him about faith and Islam, so I said to him: Differentiate between faith and Islam. He said: And shall I give you the example of it? He said: I said: I would want that. He said: The example of faith from Islam is like the example of the Sacred Kaaba from the Sanctuary; a man may be in the Sanctuary and not be in the Kaaba, and he may not be in the Kaaba until he is in the Sanctuary. Hence, he may be a Muslim and may not be a believer, and he will not be a believer until he is a Muslim. He said: Then I said: Then does anything exclude him from faith? He said: Yes. I said: Then to what thing does it turn himـ? He said: To Islam or disbelief. And he said: If a man is to enter the Kaaba and his urine slips form him, he must be taken out of the Kaaba and must not go out of the Sanctury, and if he is to go out from the Sanctuary, wash his robe and purify himself, he is not prevented from entering the Kaaba. Whereas if a man is to enter the Kaaba and urinates in it intentionally, he must be taken out of the Kaaba and from the Sanctuary, and his neck is to be stricken.
